alternatives.name: cosign
alternatives.why_not_default: It signs and verifies the identity of software artifacts. It does not provide identity or provenance for equity observations. The packet card records that no signing or identity flow was run here, and that not every upstream publishes signatures. It could later sign snapshot manifests, but no evidence shows it doing so. I could not open the README URL.

alternatives.name: data-kafka
alternatives.why_not_default: It matches the replay-log scope term, but the card says a single-node synthetic replay is only a prospective smoke check, and ordering holds only within a partition. It is a transport log, not a provenance or version store. The packet's existing overturn text says to add a server only after local throughput and concurrency measurements justify it, and the evidence contains none. In the upstream metadata, the latest field is 'show' and the release date is null.

alternatives.name: foundation-socraticode
alternatives.why_not_default: It has the strongest evidence class in the packet. evidence/receipts/native-rag.json records a native_model_e2e run in which tools/ecosystem/linux-usage-report.cjs lines 2-39 were retrieved at score 0.6429, plus add, update and delete index phases. That evidence is about semantic code indexing and keeping the code index fresh. It shows nothing about identity, lineage or availability of US-equity data, so its evidence class does not carry over to this requirement.

alternatives.name: data-arcticdb
alternatives.why_not_default: It fits the versioned-store and snapshot-store terms. However, the card records a BSL-1.1 licence whose production and commercial-use terms are unresolved, and the upstream licence field is NOASSERTION. The card also says storage version time does not prove when market information was available. The evidence is source review only, with no local snapshot or replay comparison.

alternatives.name: data-mlflow
alternatives.why_not_default: It covers model lineage and experiment tracking, which happen after observations are acquired and snapshotted. The card says no experiments or models were run, and that autologging does not capture every data revision. It overlaps DVC's reproducibility role without closing the data-identity requirement.

alternatives.name: data-iceberg
alternatives.why_not_default: It fits the snapshot-store term. The card says that creating a catalog alone would not prove append, multi-writer conflict handling, cross-engine compatibility or time travel, and that storage snapshots do not show what information was available in the past. A table lake is justified only after a measured local need, and the evidence contains no such measurement.

open_gaps: No retained evidence shows DVC or OpenLineage installed, run or integrated against US-equity observations. Both winners rest on source review only.

The project-local path already hashes snapshots per file and verifies the manifest (temporal_snapshot.py lines 116-167). What DVC would add beyond Git-linked versioning of those artifacts is not established by any comparison.

The snapshot_sha256 manifest digest cannot be reproduced across reruns because it embeds a wall-clock ingested_at (temporal_snapshot.py lines 133-135; sec_data.py lines 50-51). Reproducibility therefore has to be judged on per-file and row-content hashes.

arms: c5 OpenLineage run event over the winning arm
overturn_protocol.metric: The comparison has three parts. (1) Per-file sha256 match for source.json, observations.parquet and universe.parquet, together with canonical row-content equality, under a pinned duckdb version. Ingestion metadata (ingested_at, duckdb_version) and the wall-clock-dependent snapshot_sha256 manifest digest are excluded. (2) Correct validate_source rejection of the availability-unknown or inconsistent mutations. The baseline counts only if the unittest run reports zero skips. (3) Whether the lineage event names the input dataset, the feed and the per-file content hashes.

overturn_when:
The verdict changes if an executed comparison over blueprints/us-equities/point-in-time/fixture.json shows DVC failing where another store succeeds. Each store would have to reproduce identical snapshot content and replay it, and one store would have to do this where DVC does not.

The comparison does not use the snapshot_sha256 manifest digest, because it cannot reproduce. temporal_snapshot.py lines 133-135 embed ingested_at from SEC.utc_now(), a wall-clock time with microseconds (sec_data.py lines 50-51), so the digest changes on every rerun. Instead, each arm compares:
- the per-file sha256 values in the manifest's files map (source.json, observations.parquet, universe.parquet; lines 138-139), under the same pinned duckdb version;
- the canonical row content, excluding ingestion metadata such as ingested_at and duckdb_version;
- the rejection outcomes of validate_source for rows whose availability is unknown or inconsistent.

The baseline is `python3 -m unittest tests/test_point_in_time.py tests/test_security_identity.py`, run in the pinned research SDK environment with duckdb importable. Only a run with zero skipped tests counts, because tests/test_point_in_time.py line 16 skips the whole class when duckdb is missing.

The verdict also changes if an OpenLineage event emitted for that run does not identify the input dataset, the feed and the per-file content hashes.
why_selected:
The layer is titled "Identity, provenance and lineage". Its scope terms include provenance, data-lineage, data-versioning, reproducibility and metadata-events (packet lines 284-297, 317). DVC (c2) is the adopted candidate whose packet role covers Git-linked content hashes, data dependencies and pipelines, which is the versioning and reproducibility part of the requirement. OpenLineage (c5) is the adopted open standard and client set for job, run and dataset lineage events, which is the lineage and metadata-event part. Together they cover both parts with the least overlap.

Both winners rest on source review only. The evidence is the pinned upstream READMEs: https://github.com/treeverse/dvc/blob/356dfa03278058b02df42124f243c2c345329dae/README.rst and https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/blob/8ad5c14c63fbab63fedd8ff42f9a208d86ad07fe/README.md. This lane could not open either URL because it has no web tool. The source-review class and the card limitations are provider judgments I kept from the packet; I did not verify them myself. No native execution, local integration or measured comparison of DVC or OpenLineage on US-equity data exists in the evidence I read.

My own source review of the project-local code found that it already covers part of the snapshot requirement. So DVC would add to that path, not replace it. In blueprints/us-equities/point-in-time/temporal_snapshot.py:
- validate_source (lines 68-113) rejects rows whose availability is unknown or inconsistent: an unsupported availability_basis (lines 90-91), availability earlier than the captured observation, event or adjustment evidence (lines 92-98), and ambiguous temporal revisions (line 111).
- write_snapshot and verified_snapshot (lines 116-167) already write per-file sha256 hashes and verify them against a manifest.

tests/test_point_in_time.py exercises this with synthetic fixtures through native DuckDB, but every test there is skipped when duckdb is missing (line 16). Neither winner is part of that path.
